title: I Posted the Cemetery Mower Quiet Hours the Crew Ignored at Dawn

parts.text: I arrived at 6:12 a.m. with flowers and the riding mower was already on the east lawn. The gate sign said: NO POWER EQUIPMENT BEFORE 8. VISITATION FIRST. Crew lead Daryl shrugged with earmuffs on. I was forty-seven, daughter, holding a visiting-hours card. "Crews are visitation of the grass." I photographed the time, the sign, and the mower serial. Then I posted the stills to the cemetery board email. At 6:20 the superintendent asked why Daryl's serial was on a quiet-hours ticket. I waited where the camera already was.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The superintendent can see Daryl's mower serial on a 6:12 quiet-hours still.

social.video_title: They mowed at 6:12 under an 8 a.m. sign — Part 1/2
social.description: Cemetery, a dawn mower, and a gate sign the crew walks past. I posted the stills. Would you have waited for 8?

parts.text: Daryl called it dew until the superintendent asked for the ticket. I printed the stills, the sign, and the serial. The mower parked. He started at 8:01 and told the crew dew was always about optics. Optics is a word crews use when a serial exists. Quiet hours now have a second line: GRASS IS NOT VISITATION. I keep a visiting card. Daryl waits for eight. The lawn finally sounds like morning, not a engine. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: Ticket, parked mower, and a second line. Was dew ever 6:12?
